chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Victor Young hires him for the Maytag program
summary: Walking down Randolph Street he meets Victor Young, who has been seeking a jazz xylophonist for the Maytag show; they had met at the Uptown Theater.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, but they wouldn't leave town. They liked it there. Anyway, I went to Chicago and I'm walking down Randolph Street and I walk into Victor Young. And that's when he started up --
Well did you know him?
Oh, yeah from (unintelligible), he was a violin player. At the Uptown Theater, I told you when I was doing a single, that's when I met him.
Oh, yes. I see. Yes, right.
So he said he thought I 'd belong in Chicago. Cause I was always working at Publix Theaters, see few years ahead.
Yeah, yeah.
He said, "I've been looking all over," he said -- I said "Why?" He said, "I got the Maytag Program and I'm looking for somebody that can play jazz like you."
Because -- you know that when you were with Paul Ash?
Yeah, he saw -- that's when I was with Paul Ash and I was doing a single.
Yeah.
So I worked the Uptown Theater and he was a violin player.
I see, yes. I get it.
He just written a song called "Sweet Sue," which was a big hit in Chicago, at that time. And --
And he was just a first violin player?
No, he was a violinist. I don't know if he was first -- he was in the section, that had four or five other violinists in the band.
Heaven's sake.

In Benny Kruger's band. So then he had spent a time after that working at WGN. He'd left the theater and he was directing Goldkett's band at WGN. They had to be on account of Sunday night. And I played at a couple times with him, you follow me?
Yeah.
I played there a couple of times with him, so he knew my work.
Yeah.
So this was before the Merchandise was up, and we did -- NBC was in the Capitol Building on State and Randolph there, at the top --
Yeah, yeah.
-- there's a big studio up there. So, I just started working with him on that one day a week. I just loved it because it was great musicians in the band.
Yeah.
